claims.claim: Fast mode for Claude Opus 5.5 no longer needs a beta header or access request. It costs $8 input and $40 output per million tokens.
claims.why_it_matters: Agent loops slowed down by output can opt in per request at a known premium price (per Anthropic's docs, not on the Batch API or Claude Platform on AWS). Anthropic's speedup figure is its own claim.
claims.try_this: Fast mode bills at premium rates and switching speed invalidates the prompt cache, so try it on one existing Opus 5.5 request: add speed: "fast" and check usage.speed in the response.

verification.method: Anthropic fast mode docs confirm no beta header for Opus 5.5 and $8/$40 pricing; 2.5x speed is Anthropic's own figure

claims.excerpt: Fast mode runs the same model with a faster inference configuration. There is no change to intelligence or capabilities.

claims.claim: Claude Code v2.1.302 turns fork subagents on by default in claude -p, the Agent SDK, the desktop app and VS Code. Setting CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 turns them off.
claims.why_it_matters: Headless and SDK pipelines may now spawn fork subagents they did not before, which can change cost and behavior.
claims.try_this: If you run claude -p in CI, pin the version or set CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 until you have compared output and token use.

verification.method: Read official GitHub release notes for v2.1.302; no sandbox run

claims.claim: Claude Code v2.1.302 adds a notice saying standalone Claude Design at claude.ai/design will close by December 14, 2026.
claims.why_it_matters: Teams using standalone Claude Design have a fixed date to move their work or workflows elsewhere.
claims.try_this: List any design work stored only in claude.ai/design and plan to export it before December 14, 2026.

verification.method: Anthropic's own release notes state the closing date; scored at deadline

claims.excerpt: Added a notice to /design-sync and /design-login that standalone Claude Design (claude.ai/design) closes by December 14, 2026

claims.claim: Codex CLI 0.163.0 runs independent read-only tools in parallel, lets you send a follow-up to steer Codex while it is still responding, and adds a searchable /config panel.
claims.why_it_matters: Parallel lookups and steering mid-turn cut wait time and wasted turns in long agent sessions.
claims.try_this: After upgrading, send a short correction while a long Codex turn is running and see whether it changes course without restarting.

verification.method: Read official openai/codex GitHub release notes for 0.163.0; no sandbox run

claims.excerpt: Codex can run independent read-only tools in parallel, including skill, memory, and conversation-history lookups.

claims.claim: Cursor released an Environments API in beta for creating and managing cloud agent environments in code. Environments now hold up to 300 repos.
claims.why_it_matters: Teams can script agent environments for big multi-repo setups instead of configuring them by hand. Cursor's load-speed figure is its own claim.
claims.try_this: Read the Environments API beta docs and list which of your repos one shared agent environment would need.

verification.method: Cursor's changelog confirms API beta and 300-repo limit; 5x speed is Cursor's own figure

claims.excerpt: Cloud agent environments now support up to 300 repositories.

claims.claim: Claude Code Review, which reviews GitHub pull requests on Anthropic's infrastructure, is available on Team and Enterprise plans. It has Quick, Standard and Deep levels, and it never approves or blocks a PR.
claims.why_it_matters: Gives teams a managed reviewer with a cost dial per repo that cannot gate merges by itself.
claims.try_this: If an org Owner has enabled Code Review (each review is billed), add a REVIEW.md at the root of one repo's default branch describing what to flag, then comment @claude review (you need write access to the repo). If the repo also runs the Claude Code GitHub Action, that comment may trigger it too.

verification.method: Claude Code docs confirm Team/Enterprise availability and the three review levels; no hands-on run

claims.excerpt: A review never approves or blocks the pull request, so the decision to merge stays with your team.

claims.claim: Perplexity open-sourced SPACE under Apache 2.0. It is a sandbox platform that runs code in isolated Firecracker microVMs, meant for agent execution environments.
claims.why_it_matters: A permissively licensed, self-hostable option for isolating code your agents run.
claims.try_this: Read the SPACE README and compare its isolation model with the sandbox your agents use now; do not deploy without your own review.

verification.method: GitHub repo exists, README and Apache 2.0 license confirmed; isolation not tested by us

claims.excerpt: a sandbox platform for running code in isolated Firecracker microVMs

claims.claim: Claude Code v2.1.301 adds classifier_verdict and permission_mode to OpenTelemetry tool_decision events. This lets you tell auto mode classifier decisions apart from permission rule decisions.
claims.why_it_matters: Teams auditing agent permissions can now tell whether each tool decision came from the auto mode classifier or a permission rule.
claims.try_this: If you export Claude Code telemetry, add a dashboard filter on classifier_verdict to count classifier blocks separately from rule denials.

verification.method: Read official GitHub release notes for v2.1.301; no sandbox run

claims.excerpt: so auto mode classifier decisions can be told apart from permission rules

claims.claim: Anthropic replaced git for its monorepo with Scion, an in-house version control system built around a server that is always online. Merges rose from about 2,500 to over 30,000 per day between May and September 2026.
claims.why_it_matters: An early sign of where git setups strain when agents write most of the code, plus ideas for server-side repo APIs. Anthropic says Scion is not a suitable replacement for git for general use.
claims.try_this: Check whether your CI jobs do full clones just to answer history questions; see whether your git host's API can answer them, or use sparse checkouts for jobs that need only some directories.

verification.method: Anthropic engineering post confirms the system and figures; internal metrics are not independently checkable

claims.excerpt: Our Scion infrastructure footprint is now 200x smaller than our previous git mirroring infrastructure in terms of CPU and memory requirements.

claims.claim: Anthropic says Claude, in a closed loop with an automated evaluator, designed better quantum circuits on eight tasks. The arXiv abstract reports significant reductions on seven of the eight. Anthropic's post says one point-addition design uses 12% more qubits but 17x fewer gates.
claims.why_it_matters: Shows a reusable pattern: a model iterating against a strict correctness checker and cost score, with little human input.
claims.try_this: For an optimization task you own, write an automated correctness check and cost score first, then let an agent iterate against them.

verification.method: Anthropic post and arXiv paper 2610.22367 exist; abstract does not name Claude; results not independently reproduced; an earlier draft of this summary (2026-10-16-57503e5e) failed the full audit and was corrected, then re-audited
verification.audit_note: Anthropic post confirms closed loop, eight tasks, 12% more qubits/17x fewer gates; arXiv abstract confirms significant reductions on seven of eight.

claims.excerpt: Compared with the smallest previous design, one circuit in the family uses 12% more qubits but 17x fewer gates.

claims.claim: Anthropic reports that Claude worked out how the NIST P-curve seeds were generated: lrand48 seeded with Unix timestamps from 1997 to 1998, not a hash. Anthropic published code to reproduce them.
claims.why_it_matters: A concrete example of a model cracking a long-open puzzle by recognizing weak generator output. Anthropic says no action is needed for curve users.

verification.method: Anthropic research page confirms the claim and code; we did not run the reproduction
verification.audit_note: Anthropic page confirms lrand48 seeded with Unix timestamps (May 1997–April 1998), not a hash, and published reproduction code.

claims.excerpt: the output of the C library’s lrand48 random-number generator, seeded with a Unix timestamp!

claims.claim: Anthropic gave six METR staff access roughly like its own risk teams have. METR will publish its risk assessments; Anthropic cannot veto publication but can require redactions in set categories, and decides what falls in them.
claims.why_it_matters: Sets a public reference point for how much access independent evaluators of frontier models get.

verification.method: Anthropic's announcement page confirms six METR staff, publication rights and redaction terms

claims.excerpt: We’ve onboarded six METR employees with company hardware, office space, and access to internal tools and systems

claims.claim: Google added a Biomolecular Structure Viewer to Antigravity. It is a shared 3D view: the agent can highlight regions of a protein structure, and the researcher's highlights and pinned notes sync back to the agent.
claims.why_it_matters: An example of agent tools with a shared visual state that syncs between the person and the agent.

verification.method: Google DeepMind blog post confirms the viewer; no hands-on test

claims.excerpt: a 3D visualization tool embedded directly into Antigravity

claims.claim: Simon Willison built Chirp Pong with Claude Code and Claude Opus 5.5 Extra. It is a static web pong game for two phones that sends game state as audio chirps between the phones' speakers and microphones.
claims.why_it_matters: Shows networking over sound in a static page: the tool page says no Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or accounts.
claims.try_this: Read the published prompt on Simon's post as a template for asking an agent to build a small static web app.

verification.method: Tool page exists and describes audio-chirp play between two phones; not run

claims.claim: Addy Osmani, Morgan Westlee Lunt and Qing Wang describe how the Claude Code team reviews code. Claude reviews every change continuously, other agents verify its findings before they are posted, and human approval depends on how risky the change is.
claims.why_it_matters: It is a written, detailed review pipeline for teams where agents write most of the code, including when a human still has to approve.
claims.try_this: Read the post's section on risk-based approval, then write down which paths in your repo should always need a human reviewer.

verification.method: Read the original claude.dev post (Oct 15, 2026); authors and review flow match the quote

claims.excerpt: Now, review runs continuously, more like spellcheck while you write.

claims.claim: Claude Haiku 5.5 API pricing is $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts up to 100K tokens, and $0.50/$2.50 above that. Haiku 4.5 costs $1/$5.
claims.why_it_matters: For short prompts that is 90% cheaper than Haiku 4.5, which changes the cost of high-volume classification and sub-agent calls.
claims.try_this: Check how long your typical Haiku prompts are against the 100K-token price break before switching.

verification.method: Anthropic pricing page lists both Haiku 5.5 tiers and the Haiku 4.5 price

claims.claim: Gemini 4 Argon (gemini-4-argon) is on the paid Gemini API at intro prices of $2 input and $10 output per million tokens until November 30, 2026. From December 1 the prices are $4 and $20.
claims.why_it_matters: The price doubles after the intro period, so cost estimates for anything built now should use the December prices.
claims.try_this: Use the December 1 prices of $4/$20 per million tokens when you budget Gemini 4 Argon workloads.

verification.method: Gemini API pricing page; the 1M output-limit claim was not confirmed there and is left out

claims.claim: Claude Code 2.1.300 gzips large requests to api.anthropic.com, even when telemetry is turned off. Setting CLAUDE_CODE_GZIP_REQUEST_BODIES=0 disables it.
claims.why_it_matters: Smaller request bodies can cut latency on long sessions. The setting matters if a proxy or gateway rejects compressed bodies.
claims.try_this: If you route Claude Code through a proxy and requests start failing after upgrading, try CLAUDE_CODE_GZIP_REQUEST_BODIES=0.

verification.method: Found the changelog entry under version 2.1.300; not tested hands-on

claims.claim: Meta released open weights for Muse Spark Open, an 816B-total, 42B-active MoE with 1M context and text, image, video and audio input. Its license requires 'Built with Muse Spark Open' attribution and a separate deal for model-as-a-service businesses with over $20M revenue.
claims.why_it_matters: A large US open-weight multimodal model, but its license terms are stricter than Apache or MIT.
claims.try_this: Read the Muse Model License on the model card before you build a product on it.

verification.method: Hugging Face model card confirms specs and license terms; benchmark numbers left out as vendor claims

claims.claim: Reflection released Beam 1.0, a 501B-total, 23B-active MoE with 1M context, under Apache 2.0. It comes in BF16, FP8 and NVFP4 weights and has a published safety report.
claims.why_it_matters: A large open model under a permissive license, which is simpler for commercial use than custom model licenses.
claims.try_this: Compare the Apache 2.0 license on Beam's model card with the license of the open model you currently use.

verification.method: Hugging Face model card shows size, license and precisions; DFlash2 and Mirror CLI not confirmed there

claims.claim: StepFun released Step-5-Preview open weights, a 600B-total, 27B-active MoE with up to 1M context. It uses the StepFun Model License 1.0, which adds attribution and commercial-license conditions, not plain Apache 2.0.
claims.why_it_matters: Earlier StepFun models were Apache 2.0, so check the new license terms before using this one commercially.
claims.try_this: Read the StepFun Model License 1.0 terms on the model card before commercial use.

verification.method: Hugging Face model card confirms size, context and license; the leak claim from Reddit commenters is unverified and left out

claims.claim: A Gemini CLI change merged Oct 16, 2026 (PR #29774) adds a README note that the CLI is not optimized for Gemini 4 Argon. The PR's bot summary says the note points users to the Antigravity CLI.
claims.why_it_matters: If you use Gemini 4 Argon from the terminal, Google itself says Gemini CLI may not be the right tool.
claims.try_this: If you plan to use Gemini 4 Argon from the terminal, read the updated Gemini CLI README first.

verification.method: Merged PR page and nightly release notes; exact banner wording not visible, Antigravity pointer only in bot summary

claims.claim: Gemini CLI nightly v0.66.0-nightly.20261017 accepts a 'keys' array in keybindings.json, passes termination signals from the bootstrap parent to the child process, and checks that a binary update is actually the one on PATH.
claims.why_it_matters: These are small reliability fixes for people who script or customize Gemini CLI. They are nightly builds, not stable.

verification.method: GitHub release notes in snapshot list PRs #29773, #29790, #29757; not tested
verification.audit_note: Release notes list PRs #29773 (keys array in keybindings.json), #29790 (forward termination signals to child), #29757 (verify active binary on PATH).
